title: Blackpool Council's Project Amber imagery and AI road surveys: 5,145 potholes filled for about £450,000 and pothole claim payouts down to £719
summary: Blackpool's Project Amber imagery/AI surveys: 5,145 potholes filled for ~£450k; pothole claim payouts fell to £719 (DfT, 2024)
account: Blackpool Council's Project Amber, launched in 2019 under the Local Council Roads Innovation Group, uses high-definition road imagery to detect potholes and prioritise repairs. The Blackpool Unlimited page calls it artificial-intelligence technology piloted in Anchorsholme and Bispham and states that since summer 2019, 5,145 potholes were filled in North Shore for just under £450,000 against £1.5 million by traditional methods. The Department for Transport's release of 26 September 2024 says Blackpool was the first authority to use the technology, previously paid up to £1.5 million a year to settle pothole claims and 'last year' paid out only £719; the release date is used because 'last year' is unspecified. The reduction is credited to the whole programme, including surface treatments.
purpose: Survey road condition from imagery to find and prioritise pothole and surface defects for repair
system: Project Amber road-condition imagery and AI survey (Blackpool Council)
taxonomy_note: Closest fit; benefits are lower repair cost and fewer compensation claims. The DfT release describes an 'advanced imagery system'; the AI label comes from the Blackpool Unlimited page.

ratings.reason: General benefit without an event: programme-level figures; no identifiable individual event.

ai_role.statement: Neither source isolates the detection software's contribution: the claims reduction and savings are credited to Project Amber as a whole, which combines imagery surveys with preventive surface treatments. The Blackpool Unlimited page is undated and does not state its operator, so it is treated as a council-adjacent promotional page, not an official report.
